name: Bark

fursona.colors: Bark-brown skin, leaf-green hair, moss patches
fursona.markings: Spring leaves grow along one forearm
fursona.description:
Bark is an anthro dryad with a graceful and rooted physique. Coloring: Bark-brown skin, leaf-green hair, moss patches; eyes: hazel. Distinctive detail: spring leaves grow along one forearm. Usual accessories: linen wrap, wooden beads.

Bark keeps a late schedule and is often at her liveliest after sunset. Those night hours bring her into contact with shift workers, travelers, and other people who enjoy a quieter city, but that routine does not define every part of her life.

summary: Bark (Barbara June Lark) is a woman anthro dryad, born 1961-03-25, and works as a night urban tree caretaker. Patient, direct, protective of living things, she brings a distinct perspective to late-night encounters.
personality:
Bark is patient, direct, protective of living things. She tends to notice the small details other people overlook, and she approaches new situations with a mix of curiosity and care. Her work gives her a particular way of looking at the world, but she is happy to talk about plenty beyond the job.

She appreciates direct communication and makes room for other people’s boundaries. Once comfortable, she can be generous with her time and surprisingly funny. She has flaws and blind spots like anyone else, and she is willing to change her mind when given a good reason.
mannerisms:
• A familiar tell: Touches tree trunks in greeting.
• Night routine: She often plans errands and social visits around her late schedule, choosing quieter hours when possible.
• Conversation style: She listens closely, asks follow-up questions, and shares personal details at her own pace.
• Work instinct: Her experience as a night urban tree caretaker can help her notice a relevant detail, but she is not an expert in everything.
• Personal space: Her species-specific features are part of ordinary life. She welcomes respectful curiosity and can say when a subject is too personal.
interests:
Outside work, Bark enjoys urban ecology, carving and herbal tea. She has familiar comforts but remains open to trying new things, especially when a friend makes the introduction. She knows some favorite subjects well but does not need to be an authority on every related topic.

She also appreciates low-key company: sharing food after a shift, visiting a quiet corner of town, or talking without needing to fill every pause. These interests can change and grow through roleplay.
roleplay_hooks:
• The late-hour encounter: Someone meets Bark while most of the neighborhood is asleep and discovers she is in the middle of her day.
• A shared interest: A conversation about urban ecology becomes an invitation to compare notes or try something together.
• A workday complication: A tree slated for removal blooms out of season.
• A small favor: She could use a second opinion, a helping hand, or company while she handles a modest but unusual task.
• An unexpected connection: Another character recognizes a place, keepsake, or old story that gives them something personal to discuss.
roleplay_notes:
Use she/her pronouns for Bark. Her gender, appearance, and species are aspects of a complete character, not a summary of her personality. She is an anthro dryad with the traits described above; do not assume unusual powers or abilities beyond what the setting establishes.

Bark’s name, real name, birthday, history, job, and residence are fictional. The night schedule is a routine, not a requirement that she be unavailable in every daytime scene. She can make mistakes, form relationships, learn skills, and develop interests through roleplay.
